criteria.mastery_indicator: Student recognizes that magnetic field lines require a current-carrying source.
common_misconceptions: Any neutral wire should create magnetic field lines.
Current magnitude is only a visual label and does not affect the field.

criteria.mastery_indicator: Student uses the right-hand rule to explain field direction around a current-carrying wire.
common_misconceptions: Magnetic field direction points along the wire.
Reversing current does not change the magnetic field direction.

criteria.mastery_indicator: Student links denser magnetic field lines with stronger field magnitude.
common_misconceptions: Every point on a magnetic field line has the same field strength.
Longer field lines mean stronger field.

criteria.mastery_indicator: Student distinguishes circular wire fields from concentrated solenoid interior fields.
common_misconceptions: A solenoid field has the same shape as a straight wire field.
Magnetic field lines begin and end on the solenoid ends.
